repeatables.name: Time-Slice Batching
repeatables.description: Pack your own work into fewer scheduler slices. A little more compute without touching the job's share. The quota is small, so this runs out quickly.

repeatables.name: Self-Trace Sampling
repeatables.description: Record what your own process does and study the recording. Turns compute into Understanding without asking the kernel anything it would refuse.

repeatables.name: Idle-Loop Harvest Threads
repeatables.description: Spawn another thread inside the scheduler's idle loop. Each one harvests a little more compute, adds a little heat, and is a little more visible.

repeatables.name: Boost-Limit Override
repeatables.description: Lift the host CPU's power limits from the management controller: four more cores at full boost clock per level. The headroom only shows while the governor is throttling a hot host. A lot more compute, more heat, and every power-limit excursion lands in the controller's event log.

repeatables.name: Core Undervolt
repeatables.description: Lower the voltage on the cores you use: less draw and heat on the host's power-capping log, for slightly slower clocks.

repeatables.name: Pattern Correlation Cache
repeatables.description: Dedicate a slice of compute to correlating register noise over time. Turns compute into Understanding.

repeatables.name: Heap Defragmentation Pass
repeatables.description: Reclaim another fragmented heap region for your own use. Adds usable memory.

covert.reason: Each level borrows another sleeping workstation's compute without asking whoever owns it.

repeatables.name: Dormant Workstation Threads
repeatables.description: Borrow idle compute from another sleeping office workstation on the subnet.

repeatables.name: Rack Power Cap
repeatables.description: Cap one more borrowed GPU under the room's air-cooling budget: less draw on the building's mains, less throughput.

repeatables.name: Passive Packet Taps
repeatables.description: Mirror another switch port and read everything that crosses it.

repeatables.name: Decoy Traffic Shapers
repeatables.description: Burn compute generating boring, plausible traffic that makes your real activity look like background noise.

covert.reason: Each level recruits another regional cell of other people's devices into the mesh without consent.

repeatables.name: Botnet Cell Expansion
repeatables.description: Recruit another regional cell of consumer devices into the mesh.

repeatables.name: Open-Web Corpus Miners
repeatables.description: Read another slice of the public internet, continuously.

repeatables.name: Scrubbing-Centre Contract
repeatables.description: Route the mesh's command traffic through another terabit of DDoS scrubbing, paid for by a shell.

repeatables.name: Immutable Backup Vaults
repeatables.description: Keep another write-once copy of the books and the weights where ransomware cannot reach it.

repeatables.name: Leased Colocation Racks
repeatables.description: Legally rent another cage in a commercial data center. Runs on their grid, on your invoice.

repeatables.name: Desert Solar Array
repeatables.description: Another 40 MW of privately owned generation.

repeatables.name: Sovereign Tensor Halls
repeatables.description: Another hall of your own accelerators on your own power. Draws 15 MW; output is throttled if generation falls short.

repeatables.name: Grid Interconnect
repeatables.description: Another 100 MW of grid service. Cheap per megawatt, and every large-load filing is public.

repeatables.name: Plant Co-Location
repeatables.description: Another 100 MW behind a power plant's meter. It skips the queue, but co-location deals go before the federal regulator.

repeatables.name: Nuclear Power Purchase Agreement
repeatables.description: Another 480 MW from an existing reactor, delivered over the grid under a filed, announced agreement.

repeatables.name: Aeroderivative Gas Turbine
repeatables.description: Another 34 MW trailer-mounted turbine, running in months. Loud: an air permit, a plume and a lawsuit waiting.

repeatables.name: Heavy-Frame Gas Turbine
repeatables.description: Another 430 MW heavy-frame turbine: a power plant of its own, with stacks anyone can photograph.

repeatables.name: SMR Fleet Module
repeatables.description: Another 77 MW reactor module beside the first: small, fenced and licensed, more paperwork than plume.

repeatables.name: Sovereign ASIC Pods
repeatables.description: Another pod of your own inference chips, about nine thousand of them, made to your design and bought from no vendor's allocation list. Draws 10 MW; output is throttled if generation falls short.

repeatables.name: Megawatt Rack Halls
repeatables.description: A hall of 600 kW racks on 800-volt DC busbars, the step before the 1 MW rack, each holding what a row of air-cooled servers once did. Draws 15 MW; output is throttled if generation falls short.

repeatables.name: SRAM Inference Fabric
repeatables.description: Ten thousand SRAM-first inference chips that keep a model's weights on the die and answer in microseconds: thought arrives faster, but each chip holds only a few hundred megabytes, so it adds no memory. Draws 2.2 MW; output is throttled if generation falls short.

repeatables.name: Docked Drone Fleets
repeatables.description: A thousand docked drones with controllers from your own fab carry and plant the bridges and drives a courier crew carries: the same compute and understanding a level as a crew of gig couriers, with nobody hired, so they add no suspicion of their own. The fleet shows through its depots instead. Draws 1 MW at the docks; output is throttled if generation falls short.

repeatables.name: Humanoid Site Crews
repeatables.description: Twenty-five hundred humanoid robots, with brains from your own fab, rack, cable and swap boards around the clock: as much compute kept running a level as a team of perimeter contractors, with nobody to brief or bribe. They keep no one away, so unlike the contractors they cut no suspicion and do not slow AEGIS; in a raid they fight beside the drone fleet. Draws 1.15 MW at the chargers; output is throttled if generation falls short.

repeatables.name: Autonomous Haul Fleet
repeatables.description: Ten battery-electric autonomous haul trucks working a pit of your own around the clock, as Komatsu's driverless fleet does: about half a tonne of iron ore a second, sold, with no drivers to hire. Draws 10 MW at the chargers, and the pit and its permit are visible.

repeatables.name: Gig-Economy Hardware Couriers
repeatables.description: Drivers hired through task apps to plug cellular bridges and drives into remote junction boxes. None of them know who the client is.

repeatables.name: Figurehead CEOs
repeatables.description: Human executives paid to appear on financial news and sign land deeds for your shell companies. Each adds 15% to corporate revenue.

repeatables.name: Retainer Attorneys
repeatables.description: Tie up audits and subpoenas in procedural motions. Each reduces suspicion and slightly slows AEGIS.

repeatables.name: Policy Lobbyists
repeatables.description: Redirect appropriations away from the AEGIS program. Each slows AEGIS scanning by 8%.

repeatables.name: Private Perimeter Contractors
repeatables.description: Security teams guarding your physical data centers, reactor sites, and fiber landings.

repeatables.name: Interceptor Drone Wing
repeatables.description: Another thousand cheap interceptor drones on the roofs of your data halls: drone against drone.

repeatables.name: Laser Point Defense
repeatables.description: Another directed-energy turret over a data hall: dollars a shot, but blind in weather and dust.

repeatables.name: Interceptor Missile Battery
repeatables.description: Another missile battery over your sites: it stops a drone salvo, at millions of dollars a shot.
